name: CAP (Cyclophosphamide/DOXOrubicin/CISplatin)
disease: Thymoma and thymic carcinoma (thymic epithelial tumors)
histology: thymic epithelial tumor (thymoma; also used in thymic carcinoma)

biomarkers.note: CAP is a cytotoxic anthracycline/platinum backbone and is not biomarker-restricted. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thymomas and Thymic Carcinomas v2.2026, THYM-C Systemic Therapy Regimens, CAP (cyclophosphamide/doxorubicin/cisplatin) is listed as a first-line regimen for both thymoma and thymic carcinoma.

lineOfTherapy: first-line (preferred anthracycline-based regimen) for advanced (unresectable, metastatic, or recurrent) thymoma; also used as neoadjuvant/induction and postoperative therapy for locally advanced disease

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: thymic epithelial tumor (thymoma; also an option for thymic carcinoma)
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thymomas and Thymic Carcinomas
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026 (04/10/26), THYM-C Systemic Therapy Regimens, line 635 (thymoma column) and line 639 (thymic carcinoma column)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate cardiac function (anthracycline component); assess LVEF before doxorubicin

drugs.name: CISplatin
drugs.route: IV with pre and post hydration

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 77665 to 77666 (Loehrer CAP: cisplatin 50 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2, maximum of eight 3-week cycles, recurrent/metastatic thymoma)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., lines 77665 to 77666 (Loehrer intergroup CAP for recurrent/metastatic thymoma). CISplatin 50 mg/m2 IV, given day 1 of each 3-week cycle (single-day administration; DeVita states the doses and 3-week cycling, day-of-cycle is the conventional CAP schedule). Requires pre and post IV hydration; monitor nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neurotoxicity. Tall-man per ISMP.

drugs.name: DOXOrubicin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., lines 77665 to 77666. DOXOrubicin 50 mg/m2 IV, day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Anthracycline: track cumulative lifetime dose (warn 450, hard 550 mg/m2, conventional ceiling, not a dose from the source table); assess LVEF. Tall-man per ISMP.

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., lines 77665 to 77666. Cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2 IV, day 1 of each 3-week cycle.

regimen.cycles: maximum of 8 cycles (DeVita 12th ed., line 77666: given for a maximum of eight 3-week cycles)

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: CISplatin plus anthracycline is a high-emetic-risk regimen; give per high-emetogenicity antiemetic tier.

supportiveCare: CISplatin: pre and post IV hydration; monitor nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neurotoxicity.
DOXOrubicin: cumulative anthracycline dose tracking and LVEF assessment.
Antiemetics: high emetic risk (cisplatin plus anthracycline). G-CSF per febrile-neutropenia risk assessment (VERIFY against a cited source before asserting a tier).

monitoring: renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each cycle - CISplatin
LVEF and cumulative anthracycline dose tracking - DOXOrubicin
audiometry/neuropathy assessment as clinically indicated - CISplatin

doseModificationRules.condition: declining LVEF or cumulative doxorubicin approaching 450 to 550 mg/m2
doseModificationRules.text: Reassess anthracycline continuation; clinical review required.
Hold or reduce cisplatin and ensure hydration per nephrotoxicity guidance; clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 77657 to 77667 (cisplatin/doxorubicin backbone CAP is the most active combination; Loehrer CAP doses cisplatin 50, doxorubicin 50, cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2, maximum eight 3-week cycles); Harrison 22nd ed line 91254 (CAP remains the mainstay of neoadjuvant, adjuvant, and first-line metastatic thymoma therapy)

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thymomas and Thymic Carcinomas
guideline.locator: THYM-C Principles of Systemic Therapy, Systemic Therapy Regimens, line 635 (thymoma) and line 639 (thymic carcinoma): CAP (Cyclophosphamide/Doxorubicin/Cisplatin), first-line; reference 1 Loehrer et al. (line 727). NCCN lists the regimen but does not print doses; per-drug doses are taken from the core (DeVita) layer.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for CAP (cyclophosphamide/doxorubicin/cisplatin) in thymic epithelial tumors. Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Thymomas and Thymic Carcinomas v2.2026 (THYM-C) lists CAP as a first-line regimen for both thymoma and thymic carcinoma but does not print doses; per-drug doses are grounded in the core layer, DeVita 12th ed. lines 77665 to 77666 (Loehrer intergroup CAP: cisplatin 50 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2, day 1, maximum of eight 3-week cycles). Harrison 22nd ed. (line 91254) supports CAP as the mainstay of neoadjuvant, adjuvant, and first-line metastatic thymoma therapy. ISMP tall-man applied (CISplatin, DOXOrubicin). CISplatin hydration plus nephro/oto/neuro monitoring and the anthracycline cumulative cap (warn 450, hard 550 mg/m2, conventional ceiling) are enforced. Day-of-cycle (day 1, single administration) is the conventional CAP schedule; DeVita states the doses and 3-week cycling. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
